raw:
The modules are nearly identical. The one real difference is in the second access rule. Module A has `permitted_access_to_restricted_section(Authority, Section)`, which puts the authority in the first argument and so matches the first rule. Module B has `permitted_access_to_restricted_section(Section, Authority)`, which swaps the arguments. That is a bug in B: the first argument is the section, but the body constrains the second argument as the authority. So B's access rule for national authorities is partly wrong, although the text's meaning is still roughly there.

Sentence 1 is covered by both modules in the same way, though partially (the classification and the registration location).

Sentences 2–5 are each covered only by a generic information predicate in both modules, so both are partial and agree. The information predicates do not distinguish the individual annex points, and the rules are disjunctive over all four lists rather than tied to each sub-item.

Sentence 6 is covered by both with the same access structure. A's rule is correct. B's second rule has the swapped argument order, so the two differ on how national authorities are represented. I mark both partial, since "only" is not captured as exclusivity, and I mark agreement as "no" because of the argument swap.
